title: Every check builds the whole `Core` signature table again from the registry, which is most of the fixed floor of `nvs check`, `nvs run` and every editor analysis.
text: Measured with callgrind on the debug Linux binary, empty program, a one-block config: `nvs_types::core_lib::seed` (`crates/nvs-types/src/core_lib.rs:45`, called from `build_signatures`, `crates/nvs-types/src/check.rs:126`) is 54% of the instructions of `nvs check` and 29% of a cold `nvs run`, and dropping the table is another 8%. The table is the same for every program in one binary. `nvs lsp` pays it once per analysis: an open, one edit and one hover on an empty file ran it five times, 63% of the session (`nvs-lsp/an-edit-analyses-the-document-twice`). On the release binary an empty `nvs check` is 2.6 ms above `nvs --version`. Seeding once per process and sharing the result, for example a frozen base table and interner that each check layers its own declarations over, removes it from every check after the first. Not checked: its share of a check of a large program. Ladder: none, the cost does not grow; the floor counts in `docs/perf/performance-review.md` § floor show it.
